artworks.title: Meeting of Jason and King Aeëtes
artworks.description: Pen-and-wash study (Staatliche Graphische Sammlung München) for Carracci's Palazzo Fava frieze: Jason stands before Aeëtes, king of Colchis and guardian of the Golden Fleece. The Colchian monarch is staged as the forbidding host who will set the fire-breathing bulls and the dragon's teeth as terms of the prize.

artworks.title: Jason Taming the Bulls of Aeëtes
artworks.description: Oil on canvas (Barber Institute of Fine Arts, Birmingham): Jason yokes Aeëtes' fire-breathing bulls — the first of the Colchian king's impossible labours. De Troy's wide panel makes Aeëtes' court the arena where Medea's charms let the Greek survive the king's tests.

artworks.title: King Aeëtes
artworks.description: Quattrocento panel figure from the Argonauts-in-Colchis cycle: Aeëtes as crowned Colchian king, son of Helios and keeper of Phrixus' fleece. Florentine narrative painting gives the eastern monarch a face — the father whose daughter Medea will betray him for Jason.

artworks.title: Jason Received by King Oetes
artworks.artist: Unknown illuminator (Histoire de Jason of Raoul Lefèvre)
artworks.description: Illuminated manuscript illustration (British Library) for Raoul Lefèvre's Histoire de Jason: Jason before King Oetes (Aeëtes) at the Colchian court. Medieval romance reception keeps the eastern king as the host who greets the Argonauts — and sets the price for the Golden Fleece.

artworks.title: Aeëtes Accepts the Dismembered Corpse of Absyrtus
artworks.description: Mannerist engraving from The History of Jason and the Conquest of the Golden Fleece (Yale University Art Gallery): Aeëtes receives the scattered remains of his son Absyrtus, slain so Jason and Medea can escape Colchis. The Colchian king is shown not as fleece-keeper alone but as the father whose household Medea destroys.

films.title: Jason and the Argonauts
films.description: Harryhausen's Aeëtes is the Colchian king who sets the impossible tasks — bulls, teeth, dragon — and watches his daughter Medea choose the Greek.

films.title: Jason and the Argonauts
films.description: Hallmark's miniseries casts Frank Langella as Aeëtes — the Colchian host who greets the Argo, then hunts Jason and Medea for the stolen fleece.

popCulture.title: Argonautica
popCulture.creator: Apollonius of Rhodes
popCulture.description: Apollonius makes Aeëtes the forbidding Colchian king of the fleece quest — fire-breathing bulls, dragon's teeth, and the father Medea betrays for Jason.
